title: Karl Mayer Group turns 85
content: This year, the Karl Mayer Group turns 85 years old, and the German textile machinery leader is using the anniversary as an opportunity to pay tribute to the people behind its unparalleled success story. The new headquarters of the Karl Mayer Group in Obertshausen. What was once a family business, has developed into an international group of companies at the top of its markets. “Today, we look back on a group of companies with strong roots and business activities in the main sectors of the textile industry. The Group also continued to expand in the recent past: in 2020, the flat knitting machine manufacturer Stoll was acquired, and since 2021, the new Beyond Textile Business Unit has been committed to growth outside its traditional business areas in the textile world. In addition to the voices from the market, a new presentation on the group of companies and an anniversary video on the theme of ‘People, togetherness, insights’ will be launched.

title: KARL MAYER opens new TEXTILE INNOVATION CENTER
content: # KARL MAYER opens new TEXTILE INNOVATION CENTER. KARL MAYER opened its new TEXTILE INNOVATION CENTER (TIC) April 21 in Obertshausen, Germany. The company will be hosting an opening week for the center April 21–24, with a ribbon-cutting ceremony scheduled for April 23. “With our TEXTILE INNOVATION CENTER, we are strongly focusing on textiles as the heart of our industry and the growth engine for our customers. The center will provide a meeting space for industry members and partners to network, share ideas and learn about new developments in the industry. “The size and equipment of our new TEXTILE INNOVATION CENTER are unrivalled in the world. Here, we are aiming at the Medici effect, basically a renaissance of the textile industry; it’s about preserving and building up textile know-how and textile technology, as well as developing innovative textile solutions,” says Karl Josef Mayer, representative of the Mayer family and patron of the TIC.
